items.stem: In Julia, what does adding a dot to an operator or function call (for example x .+ 1) do?

options.text: It applies the operation element-wise across the array without building intermediate temporaries when fused
options.rationale: Correct: the dot syntax broadcasts and fuses element-wise operations, avoiding temporary allocations.

options.text: It converts the array to a different numeric type
options.rationale: Type conversion is done with functions like convert or constructors, not the dot.

options.text: It forces the computation to run on the GPU
options.rationale: GPU execution requires a GPU array type and package, not the broadcast dot.

options.text: It makes the operation run in parallel across threads
options.rationale: Broadcasting is element-wise, not automatically multithreaded.

items.explanation: Correct: the dot syntax broadcasts and fuses element-wise operations, avoiding temporary allocations.

items.stem: Which statements about multiple dispatch in Julia are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: A method can be chosen based on the types of all of its arguments, not just the first
options.rationale: Correct: Julia selects the most specific method using the types of every argument.

options.text: Adding a new method for existing types extends a function without editing the original definition
options.rationale: Correct: you can add methods to an existing generic function for new type combinations.

options.text: Dispatch is resolved only on the runtime value, never on the type
options.rationale: Dispatch is resolved on argument types, which is how specialisation happens.

options.text: Each function may define only one method
options.rationale: A generic function can have many methods for different type signatures.

items.explanation: Correct: Julia selects the most specific method using the types of every argument.; Correct: you can add methods to an existing generic function for new type combinations.

items.stem: A function shows red ::Any annotations under @code_warntype. What is the most likely consequence?

options.text: The compiler cannot specialise the code, so it runs slower and allocates more
options.rationale: Correct: type instability prevents specialisation and causes boxing and extra allocation.

options.text: The function will raise a syntax error at parse time
options.rationale: Type instability is a performance issue, not a syntax error.

options.text: The function cannot be exported from a module
options.rationale: Exporting is unrelated to type stability.

options.text: The results will be numerically incorrect
options.rationale: Results are still correct; only performance suffers.

items.explanation: Correct: type instability prevents specialisation and causes boxing and extra allocation.
